title: A protocol for rapid and parallel isolation of myocytes and non-myocytes from multiple mouse hearts
protocol: Euthanize four mice by CO2 asphyxiation and promptly pin in supine position—two per dissection board per investigator.
Place freshly prepared Perfusion buffer with enzymes in 37°C water bath.
Spray anterior thorax with 80% v/v ethanol solution to minimize fur dispersal.
Cut away a small 1–2 cm² area of skin above the intersection of the septum and diaphragm.
While holding the septum with forceps, slowly raise the ribcage.
Carefully make an incision in the abdominal cavity with surgical scissors, taking care to follow the lateral margins of the rib cage.
Hold the septum with forceps from steps 4–7.
Push away any exposed abdominal organs to reveal diaphragm if required.
Cut the diaphragm along the margin of where the diaphragm and rib cage intersect.
Pin the ribcage back adjacent to the left ear of the mouse.
Carefully remove the pericardium (if visible) from the heart gently.
Locate and cut the inferior vena cava.
Perfuse the animal with 7 mL of ice-cold EDTA buffer through the right ventricle.
Place forceps below the heart and gently raise it to expose the aorta.
Clamp the aorta using a curved hemostat securely, avoiding the atria.
With the heart clamped, cut below the hemostat to isolate each mouse heart.
Transfer the clamped heart to the perfusion platform.
Magnetically secure the hemostat in place with ventricles pointing upward.
Place a 30G needle in the apex of the left ventricle.
Start perfusion using the peristaltic pump at a rate of 1 mL/min/heart with EDTA buffer at 37°C.
Increase perfusion flow rate to 6 mL/min (1.25 mL/min/heart) once all hearts are being simultaneously perfused with EDTA buffer.
Ensure a waste reservoir is placed beneath the perfusing hearts to collect perfusate.
Periodically empty the contents of the waste reservoir into a waste beaker as it fills.
Periodically baste the surface of the hearts using a Pasteur pipette with clean pre-warmed EDTA buffer to prevent tissue from drying out.
Perfuse hearts with EDTA buffer until blood is no longer dripping into the waste reservoir (∼5 min after start).
Switch buffers from EDTA buffer to Perfusion buffer with enzymes and resume perfusion at 6 mL/min (1.25 mL/min/heart).
Baste hearts undergoing perfusion with pre-warmed Perfusion buffer with enzymes until they appear slightly blanched, translucent, and dilated (∼30 min).
Prepare a 30 mm petri dish with 1 mL of Perfusion buffer containing enzymes.
Prepare a 50 mL tube with 2 mL of Perfusion buffer containing enzymes.
Cut between the atria and ventricles using curved scissors to collect cardiac ventricles in the petri dish when digestion is complete.
Gently pull apart tissue within each petri dish using forceps at ambient temperature.
Aspirate the released cells using a 3 mL Pasteur pipette.
Transfer the suspension into the 50 mL tube containing RT Perfusion buffer.
Triturate gently 10 times in the 50 mL tube with a Pasteur pipette.
Place the 50 mL tube in a 37°C water bath with caps loosely tightened for 5 minutes.
Pipette mix the contents of the 50 mL tube 15 times using a Pasteur pipette.
Place the 50 mL tube back in the 37°C water bath and incubate for another 5 min.
Aliquot 5 mL of cold Stop buffer to a fresh 50 mL tube per heart and place on ice.
Gently pipette-mix the cardiac cell suspension using a Pasteur pipette for another 15 times.
Filter the cell suspension through 177 μm nylon mesh into the pre-prepared 50 mL tube containing Stop buffer.
Leave the filtered cell suspension on ice, undisturbed, for 10 min.
Centrifuge the cell suspensions at 50×g for 2 minutes at 4°C.
Prepare 15 mL tubes with 7 mL of cold wash buffer per heart and place on ice.
Place tubes containing the supernatant and pellet on ice after centrifugation.
Transfer all but approximately 1 mL of supernatant to the 15 mL tubes through a 70 μm nylon mesh into the wash buffer and place on ice.
Top up the volume of non-myocyte enriched samples to 15 mL with cold wash buffer.
Centrifuge the top-up samples at 200×g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the samples after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet containing non-myocytes in a desired buffer depending on subsequent application.
Add 5 mL of cold Stop buffer to the cardiomyocyte pellet in the 50 mL tube.
Gently resuspend the pellet with the Stop buffer.
Spin down cardiomyocytes an additional time at 50×g for 2 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from the sample after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet in a desired buffer.
Place the 50 mL tube back in the 37°C water bath and incubate for another 5 min.
Aliquot 5 mL of RT Stop buffer to a fresh 50 mL tube per heart and leave at room temperature (RT).
Gently pipette-mix the cardiac cell suspension using a Pasteur pipette another 15 times.
Filter the cell suspension through 177 μm nylon mesh into the pre-prepared 50 mL tube containing Stop buffer and leave undisturbed for 10 min.
Centrifuge the cell suspensions at 50×g for 2 min at RT (with centrifuge breaks activated).
Prepare 15 mL tubes with 7 mL of cold wash buffer per heart and place on ice.
Transfer all but approximately 1 mL of supernatant to the 15 mL tubes through 70 μm nylon mesh into the wash buffer and place on ice.
Top-up the volume of non-myocyte enriched samples to 15 mL with cold wash buffer.
Centrifuge at 200×g for 15 min at 4°C with centrifuge breaks deactivated.
Remove the supernatant.
Re-suspend the pellet (containing non-myocytes) in a desired buffer depending on subsequent application.
Add 10 mL of RT Stop buffer to the cardiomyocyte pellet in the 50 mL tube after removing the supernatant.
Gently re-suspend the pellet at room temperature (RT).
Spin down cardiomyocytes an additional time at 20×g for 3 min at RT with centrifuge breaks activated.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Re-suspend in a desired buffer.

If cardiomyocytes are to be used for applications such as cell culture, incubate them sequentially in Myocyte Wash Buffers containing increasing concentrations of Ca2+ (Myocyte Wash Buffer 1: 0.18 mM; Myocyte Wash Buffer 2: 0.45 mM; Myocyte Wash Buffer 3: 1.08 mM).
Plate the myocytes in Plating Media containing 1.26 mM Ca2+.
Resuspend cardiomyocytes in 10 mL Myocyte Wash Buffer 1.
Transfer cell suspension to a 70 mL specimen jar and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Transfer cells to a 14 mL round-bottomed tube and centrifuge at 20×g for 3 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate supernatant, leaving ∼50–100 μL so as not to disturb the pellet.
Resuspend cardiomyocytes in 8 mL Myocyte Wash Buffer 2, transfer to a 70 mL specimen jar and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Transfer cells to a 14 mL round-bottomed tube and centrifuge at 20×g for 3 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate supernatant, leaving ∼50–100 μL so as not to disturb the pellet.
Resuspend cardiomyocytes in 10 mL Myocyte Wash Buffer 3, transfer to a 70 mL specimen jar and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Transfer cells to a 14 mL round-bottomed tube and centrifuge at 20×g for 3 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate supernatant and gently resuspend cardiomyocytes in the desired volume of Plating Media (e.g., 5 mL for a 60 mm tissue culture dish).
Immediately aspirate laminin from cell culture plates, wash with sterile PBS without Ca2+ Mg2+ and gently add cardiomyocytes in Plating Media to the dish.
Incubate plates at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 1 hour to allow cells to adhere.
Replace Plating Media with Maintenance Media and incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 for an additional 1.5–2 hours prior to performing any treatments.
